summary: Feature: the sketch origin and the H and V axes are fixed elements that every sketch relation can name, as the point @origin and the lines @h and @v. They are never stored, and the @ prefix is reserved: a stored point, edge or relation id that starts with @ is refused. Relations reach them through their operand signatures, as any other point or line: Coincident places a point at the origin or on an axis, Midpoint keeps the origin at the middle of a line, Parallel, Perpendicular and Collinear take an axis as a line, Symmetric mirrors about an axis and mirrors the origin about a line, Distance, the point-to-line distance and Angle measure from the origin or an axis, a new Tangent keeps an arc or circle touching an axis on the side its centre starts on, and Concentric and Coincident centre an arc or circle on the origin or keep the origin on one. What an axis lacks is a capability, so Equal, a line and arc Tangent and Midpoint on an axis, and Fix on the origin, are refused with the reason, and a relation whose operands are all fixed is refused. A condition another kind already keeps is stored only in that kind, its canonical form: a point at the origin, on an axis, level or upright with the origin, or mirroring the origin about an axis is a fixed coordinate at 0, a line parallel or perpendicular to an axis is Horizontal or Vertical, a line collinear with an axis holds both ends at 0, and a distance from an axis or along one from the origin is a signed fixed coordinate. The planner plans that form and recognises it as already applied, and a parse refuses the other form, naming the one to store. The lowering gives the fixed coordinates as sentinels: an equation on them takes a simpler form where one exists, and otherwise their values become fixed parameters made once, through the lowering context, which refuses what an axis cannot give with its typed refusal. The datum special cases are deleted: the datum pick type, datum-only planning, the datum labels and glyph naming, and the panel's position-from-the-origin command, which the Dimension tool replaces. The canvas still draws the axes and the origin; picking one gives an ordinary selection that the selection set, the relations panel, highlights, snaps and agents share, labelled Origin, H axis and V axis. A point and the origin take a Distance, or a horizontal or vertical distance that holds the point's coordinate; a line takes its angle to an axis and its distance from the origin; Mirror copy may mirror about an axis, Trim and Extend cut at and reach the H or V axis where an agent's query names it, as infinite lines, holding a new cut on the axis at 0, while a click still cuts at drawn edges only, and a reference distance from an axis made driving becomes the coordinate it holds.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files and agents, none for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output. The sketch graph reserves ids starting with @: a sketch that stores such a point, edge or relation id is refused with reserved-sketch-id, whether it is opened, imported or added by an edit. A relation is non-canonical only when it names @origin, @h or @v, so every relation a sketch stores today keeps its meaning; a relation submitted with one of them in a form another kind keeps is refused (non-canonical-sketch-relation), naming the form to submit. Relation, selection and mirror operands now accept @origin, @h and @v; agents that relied on a selection set or a mirror refusing them get them accepted, and edits that would move, trim, delete, convert, offset or copy them are refused (fixed-sketch-element). Trim and Extend keep their results for existing sketches: a click, and trimAt or extendAt without axes, cut at drawn edges only, as before; an axis cuts only where a query names it in axes. The CAD format is alpha and carries no compatibility either way, so sketches saved by this release that name the origin or an axis do not open in older releases. The equation baseline of 0.0.788 is unchanged: every sketch that names neither compiles to the same equations, byte for byte. The worker protocol version stays 7.

checklist.schema: Sketch graph schema change: ids starting with @ are reserved (reserved-sketch-id), and relation operands may name the virtual @origin, @h and @v, validated by CAD_SKETCH_ELEMENT_ID_PATTERN. A new tangent relation kind keeps an arc or circle touching an axis. Trim and extend targets accept @h and @v as boundary.entityId, never as the edge they change, and a cut on an axis attaches with fixed-axis at 0. A Symmetric of the origin about an axis is stored as the fixed coordinates of its other point. Relations on the origin or an axis that another kind keeps must be stored in that canonical form (non-canonical-sketch-relation); relations whose operands are all fixed are refused (fixed-sketch-relation); an axis's missing length, ends or middle is refused (unsupported-sketch-operand). No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7 with the same buffers, and the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Agent operand change: set-sketch-relation, select-sketch-geometry-set and mirror-sketch-geometry accept @origin, @h and @v where a point or line operand is taken; the edits that change named geometry refuse them with fixed-sketch-element, while trim-sketch-entity and extend-sketch-entity accept an axis as a boundary, checked with that axis cutting, and cad_inspect_sketch_regions takes an optional axes list beside trimAt or extendAt naming the axes that also cut. A failed solve gains two start retries, after the existing ones: a fixed point held on a free curve centred on it moves the centre off it, and an arc arm held square to a support it starts along is turned a quarter to each side. A solve that succeeds first runs no retry. Looking an id up as the origin or an axis is a comparison with three constants, so it costs the same for any sketch size. Nothing new runs on pointer moves: the canvas already hit-tested and drew the origin and axes, and they now carry their ids instead of datum names. The planner's coordinate trace treats the axes as two more lines in its existing index, built once per graph.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added or removed. The set-sketch-relation edit description names the virtual operands and the canonical rule; the WebMCP discovery metadata stays within its 51,200-byte budget at 51,178 bytes after the merge with 0.0.789, after tightening the element id pattern, taking 0.0.789's shorter viewport description, and removing repetition from the region tool's description to make room for its axes field. The public agent guide documents the operands, the canonical forms, the refusals, the mirror about an axis and Trim and Extend at an axis a query names. The trim and extend edit descriptions say the axes cut only when named, and name the fixed-axis attachment; they are read through cad_describe_edits, outside the discovery metadata. Constrain lists a disabled row with its reason for what an axis or the origin cannot take, and the relation list, marks, snaps and highlights name the H axis, the V axis and the origin.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved CAD documents parse with the stricter sketch rules above; nothing is rewritten.
checklist.verification: Equation baseline: the 0.0.788 fixture replays unchanged and is not re-recorded. All 5,131 inputs give the same compiled models, native answers, graph-check hashes, constraint inspection row hashes and solver attempts, byte for byte. For that, the fixed-axis agent meaning keeps its recorded wording ("X measured from the Y axis or Y from the X axis"); its summary names the H and V axes. Datum: git grep -i datum over src outside tests fell from 913 to 640 lines. 404 of each are the frozen PlaneGCS corpus records, and the 236 left concern 3D datum planes and frames, none sketch axes. New tests: cadSketchAxisRelations, covering each relation with the origin or an axis end to end through planning, the solve and the stored form; capability, parse, lowering and edit refusals; the mirror about an axis; reserved ids; canonical refusals for eight forms; already-applied recognition; and each lowering specialization with its exact equation. Also: the constraint tool picking the origin as a point and an axis as an edge; the dimension plan refusing the origin with an axis or a third pick; and four selectable-axes Chromium cases (Symmetric about V, Parallel to H stored as Horizontal, Concentric with the origin, Distance from H). Existing tests touched: the datum pick, preview and name expectations move to @origin, @h and @v and to the Origin, H axis and V axis names (fresh drawing, path drawing, canvas, picking, render, graph layer, placement editor, snaps, glyph layout, dimension selection, placed dimension layout, constraint feedback, presentation, registry mention). The constraint tool, dimension placement, relations panel and workbench suites follow the canonical forms and the point-and-origin Distance. The relation baseline maps the retired datum names to their new ones by name and compares every other recorded value as recorded. cadSketchLowering passes the new parameter count. The datum preparation test is renamed for axes. The panel's position-from-the-origin and datum-reuse tests go with that command; the Dimension tool's tests cover their cases. Review round 1 added: cadSketchAxisRelations grows to 21 tests, covering the origin mirrored as a point, tangent to an axis from a centre on it, a tangent joint from a centre on its fixed line, a fixed point on a free curve centred on it, values in the already-applied check and reserved ids on every load path. cadSketchAxisReaders (5) reads a sketch that stores every relation form with a virtual operand through each reader: parse and the JSON round trip, DXF export, the graph check, cad_measure_sketch, constraint inspection and paging, operand labels, highlights and placement, diagnosis marks, dimension and glyph layout, the measurement reader, the reference-to-driving conversion and its lock, region inspection and cad_read_features. cadSketchAxisTrim (6) shows that a click, and trimAt or extendAt without axes, cut at drawn edges only, giving the earlier exact target for a circle centred on the origin under a chord, and that an axis named in axes cuts as an infinite line with its fixed-axis attachment, with stale witnesses, axis targets and malformed axes lists refused. cadStorage refuses a stored reserved id on both adapters without writing, and cadSiteTools checks the axes field before any controller access. No existing trim or extend test changed. Mutations, each restored: answering only the H axis in the constant-time lookup fails 17 tests in 3 files; storing a line perpendicular to an axis as Horizontal fails 5 in 2 files; and swapping the kept coordinate of the symmetric specialization fails the mirror test. Round 1 mutations, each restored: an unsigned axis tangent fails 2 of 21; dropping the quarter-turn starts fails 1; a retry that moves only the point fails 1; named axes that never cut, edits that ignore the axes their target names, and an axis refused as a boundary each fail 3 of 6 in cadSketchAxisTrim; axes that cut by default fail 4 of 72, both unchanged canvas circle trims and both click regression tests. Merge: 0.0.789 is merged into this branch, keeping 0.0.790, taking 0.0.789's viewport description, and shortening the region tool description to keep discovery at 51,178 of 51,200 bytes. Checks after the merge: the full Vitest suite passed, 6,836 tests in 583 files, including the equation baseline and the discovery budget; npm run build (tsc -b, including the e2e project, vite build, docs build and check) passed; lint has zero findings; ui:check passed; check-release passed alone and against origin/main. Chromium specs on the merged build, each run alone with two workers: cad-sketch-constraints 28, cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7, cad-sketch-dimension-selection 4, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 5, cad-sketch-axis-dimension 1, cad-sketch-dimension-placement 1, cad-sketch-circle-trim 1, cad-sketch-arc-trim 1, cad-sketch-arc-extend 1 and cad-plane-selection-section 6, all passed. No benchmark was run: no pointer-move work was added and lookups are string comparisons.

publicNotes.summary: The sketch origin and the H and V axes work in every sketch relation.
changes: Pick the origin or an axis with sketch geometry for Coincident, Midpoint, Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear, Symmetric, Concentric and Tangent, as with any point or line.
Dimension measures a point from the origin as a distance, a line's angle to an axis and a line's distance from the origin.
Mirror copy can mirror about the H or V axis.
Agents can trim at the H and V axes and extend to them by naming them; a click still trims and extends at drawn edges only.
Constrain shows what an axis or the origin cannot take, with the reason.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Sketches that name the origin or an axis do not open in older releases.
